Progress updates for 'tm' functions

Henrik Bengtsson

Source: vignettes/progressify-81-tm.md
progressify-81-tm.Rmd

The progressify package allows you to easily add progress reporting to sequential and parallel map-reduce code by piping to the progressify() function. Easy!

TL;DR 

library(progressify)
handlers(global = TRUE)
library(tm)

data("crude", package = "tm")

docs <- tm_map(crude, content_transformer(tolower)) |> progressify()
tdm <- TermDocumentMatrix(docs) |> progressify()

Introduction

This vignette demonstrates how to use this approach to add progress reporting to tm functions such as tm_map() and TermDocumentMatrix().

The tm package is a framework for text mining. Its functions process each document in a corpus. For example,

library(tm)
data("crude", package = "tm")
docs <- tm_map(crude, content_transformer(tolower))
docs <- tm_map(docs, removePunctuation)
tdm <- TermDocumentMatrix(docs)

For large corpora, these steps can take a long time without any feedback on how far they have progressed. We can easily add progress reporting by using:

library(tm)

library(progressify)
handlers(global = TRUE)

data("crude", package = "tm")
docs <- tm_map(crude, content_transformer(tolower)) |> progressify()
docs <- tm_map(docs, removePunctuation) |> progressify()
tdm <- TermDocumentMatrix(docs) |> progressify()

Using the default progress handler, the progress reporting will appear as:

  |=====                    |  20%

Supported Functions

The progressify() function supports the following tm functions:

  • tm_map() for VCorpus objects
  • TermDocumentMatrix() and DocumentTermMatrix() for VCorpus and PCorpus objects
  • tm_index()

These are the functions that process documents via the tm tm_parLapply() function. Note that tm_map() with lazy = TRUE defers the processing until the documents are accessed, which is outside the scope of progressify(). The SimpleCorpus objects created by Corpus() for vector sources are processed without tm_parLapply(). Use VCorpus() instead to get progress updates.

Limitations

The progressify() function cannot yet be combined with futurize() of the futurize package for tm functions, because both work by setting the tm_parLapply_engine() option, which only one of them can control. With |> progressify() |> futurize(), the processing is parallel, but there is no progress reporting. With |> futurize() |> progressify(), there is progress reporting, but the processing is sequential.
